newsitem.title: USA: Raines sworn in as U.S. budget director.
newsitem.headline: Raines sworn in as U.S. budget director.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore officially swore in Franklin Raines as director of the Office of Management and Budget in a private ceremony Friday, OMB announced in a statement.

The statement quoted Raines as saying he looked forward to helping President Clinton and the vice president "as they continue the important work of balancing the budget while protecting the priorites that matter most to hard-working Americans."
If Clinton is re-elected, Raines will have the task of preparing the president's budget proposal for fiscal 1998. The president's budget is usually released early in the year.
Raines was confirmed by the Senate Sept. 6 and assumed the job a few days later. He succeeded Alice Rivlin, who left the post in June to become vice chairwoman of the Federal Reserve Board.
